definition: Scintillating means sparkling with quick, dancing points of light — and, of lively talk or wit, flashing with the same brilliance.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word scintillating. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know scintillating should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The chandelier's ten thousand crystals kept the ballroom scintillating through the last waltz.
Gleaming is one steady, soft shine — a well-kept floor; it stops far short of scintillating.
Glinting goes further than gleaming — a hard flash now and then — but stops short of scintillating, an unbroken shower of sparks.

Sparkling is the everyday twin — quick points of light dancing off water, glass, or lively talk. Scintillating means the same motion with more polish and more voltage: the sparks come thick and fast, and the word itself dresses up, especially for brilliant conversation. Cider sparkles; a great wit scintillates.

Glittering is hard, bright flashing — sequins, frost, a case of diamonds — and it can feel cold or even suspect, as in glittering prizes. Scintillating keeps the flash but warms it with life and wit. Glittering light impresses the eye from a distance; scintillating light, or talk, delights the company.

Scintillating is precise in both senses at once: literally, light broken into quick dancing points; figuratively, wit that flashes the same way.
Steady brilliance would be radiance — scintillating is brilliance that keeps sparking.
